label: Code lines change, last 20 PRs
means: Whether the code grew or shrank over the latest merged pull requests.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: the code holds or shrinks over the last merged PRs, so it stays as small and simple as it can. No outside standard
source: last N merged PRs: code lines now against main just before its last params.merged_prs merged PRs, counted from git's tree with the same rules (git log --first-parent of origin/<branch>, then <branch>, then HEAD, where the branch is ci.json's params.default_branch, else params.main_branch; with neither, HEAD; ls-tree, cat-file); detail is lines added less removed per area. N is params.merged_prs, 20 by default: a repo sets it so N merged PRs turn over within hours at its own merge rate

params.bytes_per_token_source: Measured 2026-11-10 on quality/collectors/code/code.test.mjs: 83,363 bytes, which Claude Code's Read tool counted as 35,495 tokens, 2.35 bytes a token for code. The bytes over four estimate gave 20,841, 1.7 times too few. One definition: code.largest_file_tokens reads it too

label: Files over 300 lines
means: Files so long that they are hard to read in one sitting, in every language, stylesheets included.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: no file over the limit. The limit, params.limits.file_lines (300), is the default of ESLint's max-lines rule (eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/max-lines)
source: state: code lines per .ts, .mjs, .astro, .css, .py and .sh file in params.areas; a comment or a Python docstring is not a code line (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

label: Functions over 50 lines
means: Pieces of code too long to understand at a glance.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: no function over the limit. The limit, params.limits.function_lines (50), is the default of ESLint's max-lines-per-function rule (eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/max-lines-per-function)
source: state: TypeScript compiler API, and Python's ast through one python3 -I call, code lines per function in params.areas (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

label: Functions over complexity 10
means: Pieces of code with so many branches that they are hard to test and change.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: no function over the limit. The limit, params.limits.complexity (10), is McCabe's (A Complexity Measure, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, 1976)
source: state: TypeScript compiler API over .ts, .mjs and .astro script blocks, and Python's ast over .py files through one python3 -I call, in params.areas (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

label: Copied code
means: How much code is copied and pasted instead of shared. Copies drift apart.
goal_source: goal: duplication in new code of 3.0% or less, a condition of SonarQube Server 2026.5 docs, Introduction to quality gates, the built-in Sonar way gate (docs.sonarsource.com, read 2026-11-04); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: runs of 5+ code lines and 50+ tokens (jscpd's defaults) seen earlier in params.areas, line-based (quality/collectors/code/shape.mjs)

label: Unused files (knip)
means: Files nothing uses. They can be deleted.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: an unused file is code to read and keep that does nothing. Unused or dead code is a maintainability finding (GitHub Docs, Code Quality metrics and scores reference, docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-quality/metrics-and-ratings, read 2026-11-10); zero is a Git Crafter default
source: state: knip --reporter json, files inside params.areas

label: Unused exports (knip)
means: Code offered to other files that no file uses.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: an export no caller needs is dead code, a maintainability finding (GitHub Docs, Code Quality metrics and scores reference, docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-quality/metrics-and-ratings, read 2026-11-10); zero is a Git Crafter default
source: state: knip --reporter json: unused exports, types, enum, namespace and class members inside params.areas

label: Unused dependencies (knip)
means: Outside packages installed but never used.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: an unused package costs install time and supply-chain risk for nothing; unused code is a maintainability finding (GitHub Docs, Code Quality metrics and scores reference, docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-quality/metrics-and-ratings, read 2026-11-10); zero is a Git Crafter default
source: state: knip --reporter json: dependencies, devDependencies and optional peers in every package.json

label: Unused Python functions
means: Python functions that no code or test in the code folders calls or names. They can be deleted.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: an unused function is code to read and keep that does nothing. Unused or dead code is a maintainability finding (GitHub Docs, Code Quality metrics and scores reference, read 2026-11-10); knip reads no Python, so this metric does
source: state: each .py file's top-level functions in params.areas (Python's ast through one python3 -I call) whose name no .py file there, tests and fixtures included, reads, imports, reaches as an attribute or holds as a string; a method is not judged (quality/collectors/code/code-python.mjs)

label: TODO, FIXME and XXX markers
means: Notes about unfinished work left in the code instead of the issue tracker.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: work to do belongs in an issue, where it is tracked, not in a comment
source: state: TODO, FIXME and XXX inside comments in params.areas

label: Commented-out code blocks
means: Old code switched off but left behind. Git already keeps the history.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: git keeps old code, so a commented-out copy only misleads
source: state: 3 or more comment lines in a row that parse as TypeScript statements, in params.areas

label: References to deleted files
means: Comments and strings that point at files which were deleted or moved.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal, our own inference: a reference to a deleted file sends a reader, or Claude, to a dead end. An agent keeps file paths as references and loads each file when it needs it (Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents, anthropic.com/research/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents, 2025-09-29, read 2026-11-10)
source: state: repo paths in comments and strings in params.areas that git log shows were committed and are now gone (needs full history: fetch-depth 0)

label: Shared functions with a header comment
means: Functions other files can call that say what they do in a comment or docstring right at their start.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: nearly every shared function says what it does, so Claude can use it without reading its body. Python's own rule is that all functions a module exports have docstrings (PEP 257, peps.python.org/pep-0257, last modified 2024-04-17, read 2026-11-10); the 90% is a Git Crafter default
source: state: exported functions in params.areas with a comment ending on the line above (TypeScript compiler API), and each .py file's public top-level functions with a docstring or such a comment (Python's ast)

label: Files that open with a purpose comment
means: Code files that start by saying why they exist.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: every file says why it exists, so Claude reads the purpose before the code. No outside standard
source: state: code files in params.areas whose first thing, after any shebang or .astro fence, is a comment of 3+ words besides tool directives (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

label: Files and folders named by convention
means: Files and folders named the way their neighbors are, so they are easy to find.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: every code file and folder follows its folder's convention. No outside standard for the share; Python's own convention is short, all-lowercase module names (PEP 8, peps.python.org/pep-0008, read 2026-11-10)
source: state: git ls-files in params.areas, each code file and each folder holding one against the first rule in params.naming whose path pattern matches it, a folder as its path ending in a slash (quality/collectors/code/shape.mjs); by default .astro components PascalCase, pages kebab-case or [param], .py and .sh snake_case, other code and folders kebab-case

label: Code areas drawn in a README
means: Code folders that a README, or a doc it links, shows in a table or a diagram, so a reader sees the layout.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: every code area is drawn where a reader lands. A README tells people about a project, and GitHub renders Mermaid diagrams in Markdown (GitHub Docs, About the repository README file, and Creating diagrams, read 2026-11-10); the share is a Git Crafter default
source: state: git ls-files: each area in params.areas named as a folder, its path ending in a slash, in a table row or a mermaid block of a README.md above it or of a Markdown doc that README links in its own folder, or holding a README.md with a table or a diagram of its own (quality/collectors/code/code-structure.mjs)

label: Import cycles
means: Groups of files that import each other, so none of them can be read, tested or changed alone.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: no import cycle. In a cycle a module might not have finished executing when it is returned (Node.js v26 docs, Modules: CommonJS modules, Cycles, read 2026-11-10), and low coupling is what Microsoft's code metrics ask for (Microsoft Learn, Code metrics values, updated 2026-10-20, read 2026-11-10)
source: state: relative imports and re-exports of each .ts, .mjs and .js file in params.areas (TypeScript compiler API) and sibling-module imports of each .py file; strongly connected groups of two or more files (quality/collectors/code/code-cycles.mjs)

label: Line and branch coverage
means: The share of code lines and branches the automated tests run, together, close to how SonarQube counts coverage.
goal_source: goal: new code test coverage of 80.0% or more, a condition of SonarQube Server 2026.5 docs, Introduction to quality gates, the built-in Sonar way gate (docs.sonarsource.com, read 2026-11-04). SonarQube coverage mixes lines and conditions, coverage = (CT + LC)/(B + EL) (SonarQube Server 2026.5 docs, Metric definitions, read 2026-11-04), so branches count beside lines. v8 counts true and false branch outcomes apart, where that formula counts true once, so the share approximates SonarQube coverage rather than matching it; the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: vitest v8 coverage, json-summary, or for a params.test_suites suite with runner node, the node --test --experimental-test-coverage lcov its CI job printed (code-lcov.mjs), read from that workflow's newest successful run on the default branch; in ci mode only: covered lines plus covered branches over all lines plus branches of each suite's cover folders, suites summed, never averaged; lines only, with the suite named, when a report has no branch data. node counts only the files a test loads

label: Slowest recent Worker request
means: How long the Workers took on their slowest recent request since the latest deploy, from start to finish.
goal_source: goal: web.dev's good time to first byte, 0.8 seconds or less, and poor above 1.8 seconds (web.dev/articles/ttfb, updated 2025-11-28, read 2026-11-04), held by even the slowest recent request; the Worker's own time is one part of it
source: last N requests: cf workers deployments list per Worker in params.workers (the first is the one serving traffic), then cf sql query on logs.workersLogs, the newest params.last_requests fetch invocations since that deploy; the largest wallTimeMs, worst Worker; local mode only. N is params.last_requests (100 by default): a repo sets it so that many requests turn over within hours at its own traffic

label: Heaviest recent Worker request, CPU
means: Server work time of the heaviest recent request since the latest deploy.
goal_source: goal: Workers Free's CPU limit of 10 ms per request, which every request must stay under, the heaviest included (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits, updated 2026-10-29, read 2026-11-04); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: last N requests: cf workers deployments list per Worker in params.workers, then cf sql query on logs.workersLogs, the newest params.last_requests fetch invocations since that deploy; the largest cpuTimeMs, worst Worker; local mode only. N is params.last_requests (100 by default): a repo sets it so that many requests turn over within hours at its own traffic

label: Largest Worker bundle, gzipped
means: Size of the server code Cloudflare loads. Smaller starts faster.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal. No outside standard: Cloudflare sets no compressed size limit and caps a Worker at 64 MiB uncompressed (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits, read 2026-11-03)
source: state: wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir <tmp> in each folder of params.workers; gzip of the bundled modules; the largest Worker

label: Client JS per page, gzipped
means: Script a visitor's browser downloads on the heaviest page.
goal_source: goal: 0.3 MiB (307 KiB) of JavaScript, the JS share of a JS-light page's critical-path budget for a 3 s load on the 75th-percentile phone and network; near is 0.62 MiB (635 KiB), the JS-heavy page's share (Alex Russell, The Performance Inequality Gap, 2026 (infrequently.org, published 2025-11-24, updated 2025-11-28, read 2026-11-04))
source: state: the built static site in params.client_dist.dir: each page's first-party scripts, modulepreloads and their imports, gzipped; heaviest page. A build older than the newest commit touching params.client_dist.source is not measured

label: Worker build time
means: How long the server code takes to bundle.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: a quick bundle keeps the push gate quick. No outside standard
source: latest: wall time of wrangler deploy --dry-run for each folder of params.workers, this run

label: Check job wall time
means: How long the check every change waits on runs.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: the ten-minute build, "For most projects, however, the XP guideline of a ten minute build is perfectly within reason" (martinfowler.com/articles/continuousIntegration.html, updated 2024-01-18); near is twice it
source: latest: wall time of params.check's job in its workflow's newest successful run on the default branch; detail is that job in each of the newest successful runs

label: Code a session reads, largest area, in tokens
means: The largest area's code, tests included, as tokens a session loads to read that area whole.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: one area fits a 200k-token context window, the smallest Claude still serves; near is the 1M largest, and recall degrades as context grows (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows, read 2026-11-03). An agent keeps lightweight references and loads files just in time with its tools, so a session reads the area it works in (Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents, anthropic.com/research/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents, 2025-09-29, read 2026-11-04)
source: state: bytes of the code files in each area of params.areas, tests included, over params.bytes_per_token; the largest area. An area leaves out any folder that is an area of its own

label: Largest code file, in tokens
means: The biggest code file, tests included, as tokens a session loads to read it whole.
goal_source: goal: one Read call returns at most 25,000 tokens by default, so a larger file is read a page at a time; near is 111,500 tokens, the 256 KB past which Read refuses a whole file, at params.bytes_per_token (2.35) bytes a token (Claude Code Docs, Tools reference, code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, read 2026-11-10)
source: state: bytes of the largest code file in params.areas, tests included, over params.bytes_per_token; detail is the ten largest

label: Worker startup time, latest deploy
means: How long the deployed Worker takes to load its code before it can answer, as Cloudflare measured it.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal, 2026-11-04: a fifth of Cloudflare's startup limit; near is the limit itself, 1 second to parse and run the global scope, past which a deploy is rejected (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits, updated 2026-10-29, read 2026-11-04)
source: latest: per Worker in params.workers, cf workers get (its tag), cf builds list (the newest successful Workers Build) and cf builds logs get: the Worker Startup Time that wrangler deploy printed; the slowest Worker; local mode only
